synopsis: VLAct changes how a pretrained vision-language backbone learns from robot trajectories: protect early representations, train several continuous action decoders on shared features, and align compatible action coordinates across robots. The resulting backbone is transferred to a freshly initialized downstream action head. Controlled comparisons support better policy adaptation; an ablation excluding the downstream PI head provides narrower evidence for decoder-independent transfer. These are action-policy experiments, with no future-video prediction component. The supplied identifier, title, and authors match the catalog; the observed version is arXiv v1, dated August 27, 2026. [e01, e03, e04, e07, e20]

problem.text: How can continued pre-training turn limited, heterogeneous robot demonstrations into a reusable backbone? The authors identify three obstacles: erosion of broad vision-language priors, specialization to one action decoder, and incompatible embodiment-specific action coordinates.

contributions.text: A backbone-centered training recipe combines partial freezing, caption supervision, and multiple action heads; downstream evaluation discards the pre-training heads.
A partially shared action layout preserves different arm-control conventions while sharing compatible gripper supervision. Periodic joint targets and prediction residuals receive angular wrapping.

The clearest evidence for head generality is improved PI adaptation after pre-training with OFT and GR00T while excluding PI. Gains with all three heads also reflect direct exposure to the downstream decoder family.

inputs: Camera observations and a language task instruction, encoded by Qwen3-VL-4B. [e03, e10]
Demonstrated future action chunks, embodiment-dependent dimension masks, and auxiliary image-caption pairs during continued pre-training. [e04, e05, e08]
Robot state as an additional conditioning input in the GR00T-family formulation described in Appendix I.1. [e07]
outputs: Reusable backbone weights after continued pre-training. [e03]
Continuous action chunks from a selected downstream head; the pre-training layout contains 20 coordinates per action step. [e05, e07]

steps.name: Clean and align demonstrations
steps.detail: Reject invalid task labels, mask abnormal action steps, and discard heavily corrupted chunks. Delta end-effector actions are converted using dataset frame rates; joint angles are wrapped; grippers are normalized per dataset.

steps.name: Protect the inherited representation
steps.detail: Freeze the vision encoder and lower half of the language-model layers. Update upper layers with robot-action supervision and caption cross-entropy; each minibatch contains robot and auxiliary samples.

steps.name: Expose shared features to diverse decoders
steps.detail: A shared backbone forward pass produces latent z. OFT, PI, and GR00T predict the same demonstrated action chunk from this representation, and their losses are summed. OFT regresses actions directly; Appendix I describes both PI and GR00T as flow-matching generators.

steps.name: Share only compatible action coordinates
steps.detail: Coordinates 1–12 encode AgileX arm joints, 13–18 encode Franka delta end-effector pose, 19 shares Franka and AgileX-left gripper supervision, and 20 represents the AgileX-right gripper. Inactive coordinates are masked. Each decoder family shares its output layout across embodiments; the recipe still uses three decoder families.

steps.name: Transfer and specialize
steps.detail: Discard the pre-training heads and caption stream, attach a fresh task-specific head, and unfreeze the full backbone. The in-house comparisons hold downstream data, head initialization, optimizer, and training budget fixed.

training.text: The main robot mixture uses DROID and MolmoAct for Franka, and InternData-A1 and RoboCoin for AgileX. Continued pre-training uses a 4B backbone and a reported 16-GPU setup. A separate extension adds 20K UMI-style trajectories; these are not part of the default mixture.

The wrap-aware penalty is added to each head's native objective and evaluated on its final predicted action, including the generated sample for iterative heads. It applies only to absolute joint angles, excluding grippers and delta end-effector actions.
Physical evaluation trains separate single-arm and dual-arm policies for 50,000 steps on eight H800 GPUs, using 50 demonstrations per single-arm task and 100 per dual-arm task.

inference.text: OFT predicts an entire chunk in one forward pass. PI and GR00T generate continuous chunks iteratively from noise, conditioned on backbone features. Pre-training does not require deploying an ensemble of all three heads.

Robot execution is assessed through simulator episodes and physical rollouts. The supplied method does not specify a complete deployment schedule for chunk execution, observation refresh, or low-level feedback, so closed-loop timing cannot be reconstructed.

equations.expression: \begin{aligned}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{action}}&=\mathcal L_{\mathrm{OFT}}+\mathcal L_{\mathrm{PI}}+\mathcal L_{\mathrm{GR00T}},\\\mathcal L_{\mathrm{total}}&=\mathcal L_{\mathrm{action}}+0.5\mathcal L_{\mathrm{VLM\text{-}CE}}.\end{aligned}
equations.explanation: Section 3.3 sums decoder objectives; Appendix D adds auxiliary language-token cross-entropy with weight 0.5. Appendix F separately augments each decoder objective with the angular penalty.

Equations (1)–(3) canonicalize the target angle a and measure the shortest periodic residual from prediction â. Equation (4) adds this penalty to the original head loss, avoiding large regression errors across the angular boundary.

A_t is a demonstrated chunk, ε is Gaussian noise, τ is flow time, and H_t is the backbone representation. The decoder learns the velocity transporting noise toward actions. GR00T uses the same objective family with additional conditioning and a separate motor module.

results.setting: Train on standard LIBERO; evaluate perturbed test conditions with an OFT downstream head.
results.interpretation: The matched in-house gain is 7.6 percentage points. Improvement is not uniform: language-perturbation success is 81.5%, below Qwen3VL-OFT's 87.0%.

results.setting: Base: 50 clean demonstrations per task; 50 tasks and 100 evaluation episodes per task in each regime.
results.interpretation: Reported OFT results support improved clean-to-random transfer without randomized downstream demonstrations.

results.setting: Data Scaling adds 500 randomized expert demonstrations per task to the Base data.
results.interpretation: Competitive across both regimes, but not best in every column. VLAct-PI reaches 93.0% Clean; external training compute is not matched.

results.setting: Category scores average difficulty levels L0/L1/L2; the final score uses official weighting over 11 suites.
results.interpretation: The in-house improvement is 21.4 percentage points; the final average should not be recomputed as an unweighted mean of the four displayed categories.

results.setting: One policy evaluated on all 35 tasks under clean dynamic conditions.
results.metric: Success Rate / Manipulation Score, in the table's reported scales
results.interpretation: Both metrics improve, although substantial difficulty remains. Manipulation Score is distinct from complete-task success.

results.setting: RoboCasa-GR1 downstream fine-tuning; GR-1 absent from continued pre-training.
results.value: 49.5% with 20% of downstream trajectories; 54.0% with all trajectories.
results.interpretation: Supports sample-efficient adaptation to a new embodiment, rather than zero-shot control. Values are stated explicitly in Section 4.4.

results.setting: RoboDojo: 42 tasks, 50 episodes per task; August 24, 2026 leaderboard snapshot.
results.metric: Average partial-progress score / binary success rate
results.comparison: X-WAM: 7.69 / 3.83%; VLAct ranks eighth by score and sixth by success among 35 policies.
results.interpretation: These aggregate scores exceed all four explicitly designated WAM entries in this snapshot. They do not establish an architecture-level advantage under matched resources.

results.setting: Matched demonstrations and fine-tuning; 10 fixed initial configurations per task shared across models.
results.metric: Average binary completion rate, separately by task family
results.interpretation: These are physical execution results. Small per-task rollout counts limit precision.

results.setting: Table cleaning and scooping beans; scoring rewards completed task steps.
results.interpretation: Despite the paper's weighted-success terminology, these values are not binary episode-completion rates.

results.task: Transfer to an unseen action-head family
results.setting: Appendix E.1 PI fine-tuning diagnostic; PI excluded from OFT+GR00T pre-training.
results.comparison: No additional pre-training: 60.5%; OFT-only pre-training: 55.1%; all three heads including PI: 77.0%.
results.interpretation: The unseen-head gain over scratch is 2.6 percentage points. The much larger all-head result also includes direct PI-family supervision.

results.setting: Table 6 compares pre-training update strategies on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0.
results.metric: Success rate on the two benchmarks
results.value: Freeze vision encoder and lower half of LLM: 82.6% / 80.5%.
results.comparison: Update full backbone: 78.9% / 77.1%; freeze vision only: 81.3% / 79.3%.
results.interpretation: Supports the freezing recipe through downstream performance; it does not directly quantify retained vision-language capability.

results.setting: RoboTwin Base, Clean evaluation; 50 tasks with 50 training trajectories each.
results.interpretation: Controlled comparisons support both canonicalizing targets and correcting boundary residuals.

limitations.text: Decoder lock-in and preservation of VLM priors are interpretations of adaptation results. The supplied evidence does not directly establish geometric representation collapse or preserved general vision-language benchmark performance.

Published-system comparisons do not normalize training compute, optimization schedules, or checkpoint selection. They provide competitive context but weaker causal evidence than the matched in-house comparisons.
The study covers a 4B backbone; larger-model behavior is untested. RoboDojo Memory performance is particularly weak at 0.66 partial-progress score and 0.56% success.

Section 4.3 describes physical dual-arm transfer as following exclusively single-arm pre-training, while Section 4.4 and Appendix H describe a Franka-plus-bimanual-AgileX mixture. The physical checkpoint's precise pre-training subset is unresolved.
The physical study uses only 10 rollouts per task and reports no confidence intervals. Its long-horizon scores award partial credit, preventing direct comparison with binary short-horizon success.

The caption ablation has inconsistent baseline wording: Figure 8 separates Baseline 75.0, + Pretrain 79.6 and + Image Caption 82.6, while Appendix D.3 describes 75.0 as the robot-only baseline. The plot also labels a condition + Code where the prose discusses pure language instructions. The full 7.6-point improvement cannot be assigned to caption mixing alone.

The pilot Figure 2 reports OFT-to-OFT success of 75.8 on RoboTwin, while Table 9 reports 78.8 for matched OFT single-head pre-training. The paper does not clearly identify the recipe difference, so the two values should not be merged into a single baseline.

reproduction.text: Reproduction requires the Qwen3-VL-4B initialization, cleaned robot mixture, auxiliary captions, three continuous heads, masks, and angular loss. Cleaning specifies delta-action thresholds of 0.5 translation and 1.0 rotation after FPS conversion, and discards chunks with invalid-step ratio above 0.5; the gripper outlier cutoff remains unspecified.

The supplied paper does not provide a complete continued-pre-training configuration: retained dataset sizes, sampling ratios, optimizer hyperparameters, total steps, chunk horizon, generative integration steps, and random-seed uncertainty remain unresolved. GPU count alone does not establish total training cost.
Resolve caption provenance before replication: Table 7 lists LLaVA OneVision alongside LLaVA-ReCap-CC3M, whereas the accompanying caption-data paragraph names ShareGPT4V alongside ReCap.

A focused mechanism test would repeat the unseen-PI comparison with matched robot samples, backbone updates, downstream initialization, and measured compute, reporting variation across seeds. Keep PI absent from pre-training to distinguish decoder transfer from direct head-family exposure.

The abstract claims an open release while Section 4 uses future-release language; the paper’s release statements alone do not establish that the specified checkpoints and training configuration are available.

reasoning.text: The recorded VLA category and continued-training umbrella fit the described contribution. Training predicts demonstrated action chunks, and downstream inference uses an action decoder; the method specifies no future-observation model, inverse-dynamics bridge, or world-model planning loop. Joint supervision by three action heads does not establish a One Model WAM architecture. The recorded Not applicable architecture, prediction-paradigm, and quadrant fields are therefore supported as outside the WAM quadrant scheme, rather than unverified. Data augmentation is secondary to the core continued-pre-training recipe.

discussionQuestions: Would the modest unseen-PI gain persist with matched compute and repeated seeds? [e20]
Which direct representation measurements could distinguish preservation of VLM knowledge from improved optimization? [e19, e24]
Does sharing the gripper coordinate remain beneficial when embodiments have different grasp mechanics or command semantics? [e05, e23]
Can temporal conditioning improve RoboDojo Memory performance without sacrificing the backbone's transfer advantages? [e13]

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title and arXiv version line; p. 12, Authors
evidence.detail: The identifier is 2608.27550v1, dated 27 August 2026. The title and listed contributors and advisors match the supplied catalog identity.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 3–5, Sections 1–2
evidence.detail: The authors motivate reusable backbone learning under sparse robot-data coverage and interpret action-head transfer experiments as evidence of decoder specialization.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 5–6, Sections 3.1–3.2; p. 4, downstream-control paragraph
evidence.detail: Continued pre-training freezes the vision encoder and lower half of the LLM. Downstream training discards old heads and captions, initializes a new head, and unfreezes the model under controlled in-house protocols.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 6–7, Section 3.3, co-supervised multi-head pre-training and objective
evidence.detail: OFT, PI, and GR00T receive shared latent z and the same action target; their losses are summed using one shared backbone forward pass.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 7–8, Section 3.4; p. 31, Appendix I.2, Design
evidence.detail: The 20-dimensional layout allocates 12 bimanual joint coordinates, six single-arm delta-pose coordinates, one shared gripper coordinate, and one right-gripper coordinate. Inactive dimensions are masked.

evidence.location: PDF p. 27, Appendix F.1, Equations (1)–(4)
evidence.detail: Targets and prediction residuals are wrapped modulo 2π. An L1 angular penalty augments each head's native objective and is computed on final predicted actions only for absolute joint-angle dimensions.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 29–31, Appendix I.1, OFT, PI, and GR00T descriptions and equations
evidence.detail: OFT uses action-query features and direct MLP regression. PI and GR00T use conditional flow matching; GR00T's family description includes robot-state and embodiment conditioning in a separate motor module.

evidence.location: PDF p. 23, Appendix D.1–D.2, minibatch construction and total objective
evidence.detail: Every pre-training minibatch includes robot and auxiliary samples. Auxiliary VLM cross-entropy enters the total objective with coefficient 0.5.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 28–29, Appendix H
evidence.detail: The platform-specific datasets, task-label filtering, FPS-based delta-action scaling, 0.5/1.0 validity thresholds, chunk rejection above 0.5 invalid-step ratio, joint filtering and wrapping, and dataset-wise gripper normalization are specified.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Section 4 setup and Section 4.1; Table 1, VLAct, Qwen3VL-OFT, and Abot-M0 rows
evidence.detail: The setup names Qwen3-VL-4B, open robot datasets, StarVLA, and 16 GPUs. LIBERO-Plus totals are 82.6, 75.0, and 80.5; language scores for VLAct and Qwen3VL-OFT are 81.5 and 87.0.

evidence.location: PDF p. 9, Section 4.2 and Table 2
evidence.detail: Base and Data Scaling demonstration counts and evaluation protocols are distinguished. OFT results are 80.5/41.5 and 92.5/90.8; baseline results are 61.7/10.5 and 88.2/88.3. PI reaches 93.0 Clean in Data Scaling, while HoloBrain reaches 91.9/92.3.

evidence.location: PDF p. 10, Section 4.4, Setup and RoboCasa-GR1 results
evidence.detail: GR-1 and ARX X5 are absent from the stated Franka/AgileX continued-pre-training mixture. RoboCasa success is 49.5 with 20% data and 54.0 with full data; full-data Qwen3VL-OFT and GR00T-N1.6 score 48.8 and 47.6.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 10–11, Section 4.4, RoboDojo results; Table 3, VLAct and X-WAM rows
evidence.detail: The August 24 leaderboard covers 35 policies and a 42-task, 50-episode-per-task evaluation. VLAct scores 10.66/7.60 versus X-WAM's 7.69/3.83, ranks eighth/sixth, and has Memory scores of 0.66/0.56. Compute is not normalized.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 20–21, Appendix B.1; Table 4, caption and average column
evidence.detail: VLA-Arena uses within-category difficulty averaging and official weighting over 11 suites. Average success is 54.8 for VLAct, 33.4 for Qwen3-VL-OFT, and 44.3 for π0.5.

evidence.location: PDF p. 21, Appendix B.2 and Table 5
evidence.detail: One policy is tested on 35 clean dynamic DOMINO tasks. VLAct reports SR/MS of 18.50/34.20 against Qwen3VL-OFT's 10.86/30.49.

evidence.location: PDF p. 10, Section 4.3; pp. 32–33, Appendices J.1–J.3
evidence.detail: Physical tests use Franka Research 3 arms and external/wrist cameras. Separate policies train for 50k steps on eight H800 GPUs, with 50 or 100 demonstrations per task and 10 shared evaluation starts. Section 4.3 also asserts exclusively single-arm pre-training for dual-arm transfer.

evidence.location: PDF p. 33, Appendix J.3, single-arm short-horizon and dual-arm coordination paragraphs
evidence.detail: Binary success averages are 92.5 versus 77.5 for short-horizon single-arm tasks and 72.0 versus 44.0 for dual-arm tasks.

evidence.location: PDF p. 33, Appendix J.3, scoring criterion and long-horizon results
evidence.detail: Long-horizon evaluation awards partial credit for completed steps. Table-cleaning scores are 86.6 versus 73.3; scooping-beans scores are 80.0 versus 33.3.

evidence.location: PDF p. 22, Table 6 and Appendix C.2
evidence.detail: Full-backbone updating scores 78.9/77.1; vision-only freezing scores 81.3/79.3; vision-plus-lower-half freezing scores 82.6/80.5 on LIBERO-Plus/RoboTwin.

evidence.location: PDF p. 26, Table 8 and Appendix E.1
evidence.detail: PI fine-tuning scores 60.5 without pre-training, 55.1 after OFT-only, 63.1 after OFT+GR00T without PI exposure, and 77.0 after all-three-head pre-training.

evidence.location: PDF p. 26, Table 9 and Appendix E.2
evidence.detail: Head-diverse pre-training improves matched-head adaptation over single-head pre-training by 1.7, 1.6, and 4.3 points for OFT, PI, and GR00T, respectively.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 27–28, Appendix F.2 and Table 10
evidence.detail: With matched RoboTwin Base/Clean protocols, raw-angle regression scores 75.5, target wrapping 78.6, and target plus residual wrapping 80.5.

evidence.location: PDF p. 31, Appendix I.2 and Table 12
evidence.detail: Separate heads, a naively unified head, and the aligned representation score 78.5/81.1, 79.5/81.4, and 80.5/82.6 on RoboTwin/LIBERO-Plus.

evidence.location: PDF p. 23, Appendix D.2 and Table 7; p. 25, Appendix D.3
evidence.detail: Caption-source names differ between Table 7 and its accompanying prose. D.3 attributes the strongest auxiliary result to captions and discusses a 75.0-to-82.6 improvement without consistently separating the no-pre-training and robot-only baselines.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 27–28, Appendix G and Table 11
evidence.detail: A separate experiment adds 20K RealOmin UMI-style trajectories converted to delta end-effector actions, keeping the optimization budget and downstream protocol unchanged.

evidence.location: PDF p. 34, Appendix K, Limitations
evidence.detail: The authors restrict the study to a 4B backbone and leave larger-model behavior and scale-dependent recipe changes unexplored.

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, Abstract; p. 8, Section 4 setup
evidence.detail: The abstract claims models and pipelines are open-sourced, whereas Section 4 says scripts and checkpoints will be released. Neither statement demonstrates repository inspection or successful reproduction.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Figure 3; original architecture diagram visually inspected
evidence.detail: Pre-training shows the vision encoder and shallow LLM layers frozen, upper layers trainable, caption and robot inputs, and OFT/GR00T/PI supervision with a shared action layout. Fine-tuning shows a reinitialized selected head and all backbone components trainable.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Figure 4; p. 31, Appendix I.2; original diagram visually inspected
evidence.detail: The three panels contrast separate heads, naive padding into a shared head and a partially aligned 20-dimensional representation. Colors distinguish arm, gripper and inactive padding coordinates. The final layout aligns Franka gripper with AgileX left gripper while retaining separate arm blocks.

evidence.location: PDF p. 12, Figure 5(d), with Section 4.4 on p. 10; original result plot visually inspected
evidence.detail: The four downstream data fractions 10%, 20%, 50% and 100% have VLAct success labels 41.42, 49.5, 51.00 and 54.00. Full-data baseline lines are 37.0 for PI-0.5, 47.6 for GR00T-N1.6 and 48.8 for Qwen3VL-OFT. This panel concerns simulated RoboCasa-GR1 and is distinct from the physical-task panels.

evidence.location: PDF p. 25, Figure 8 and Appendix D.3; p. 23, Table 7; p. 24, Figure 7; originals visually inspected
evidence.detail: Figure 8 has separate bars labeled Baseline 75.0, + Pretrain 79.6, + BBox-QA 80.2, + Point-QA 80.9, + Code 80.6, + Spatial-QA 81.9, + Image Caption 82.6 and + Mixed Data 82.5. The prose calls the 75.0 baseline robot-only and describes pure language instructions rather than the plot’s Code label. Figure 7 shows ShareGPT4V, agreeing with the caption-data prose but differing from Table 7’s LLaVA OneVision listing.

evidence.location: PDF p. 4, Figure 2, compared with p. 26, Table 9; originals visually inspected
evidence.detail: Figure 2’s RoboTwin OFT-to-OFT bar is 75.8, whereas Table 9’s OFT single-head pre-training cell is 78.8. The supplied text does not clearly state the experimental difference behind these two same-head values, so they should not be treated as one interchangeable baseline.
